cards.statement: Cloud agility helps teams turn new business ideas into working applications quickly.
cards.explanation: On-demand resources shorten the wait for infrastructure, so teams can experiment and deliver new applications sooner.

cards.statement: Horizontal scaling increases capacity by making an existing server more powerful.
cards.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds resources, such as more servers, to share a workload instead of enlarging one server.
cards.misconception: Confusing horizontal scaling with vertical scaling.

cards.statement: Cloud elasticity matches available computing capacity to changes in workload demand.
cards.explanation: Elastic capacity follows demand in both directions, helping workloads avoid keeping resources they no longer need.

cards.statement: Deploying an application closer to its users can reduce the network latency they experience.
cards.explanation: AWS offers deployment locations around the world, allowing applications to serve users from geographically closer infrastructure.

cards.statement: High availability describes a workload's resistance to permanent loss of stored data.
cards.explanation: Availability measures the proportion of time a workload is usable, expressed as uptime relative to the total time measured.
cards.misconception: Confusing service availability with data durability.

cards.statement: Availability Zones in an AWS Region are separate sections of the same data center.
cards.explanation: Availability Zones consist of physically separate data center facilities with independent supporting infrastructure.
cards.misconception: Treating Availability Zones as partitions inside one data center.

cards.statement: Fault tolerance describes a workload's ability to operate despite a component failure.
cards.explanation: Fault-tolerant workloads use redundant components that can take over the work of a failed component.

cards.statement: Amazon RDS reduces database administration work by managing common maintenance tasks.
cards.explanation: Amazon RDS handles routine tasks such as database software patching, freeing teams to focus on their applications.

source.title: What is Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

cards.statement: Launching an Amazon EC2 instance in one AWS Region creates copies in other Regions.
cards.explanation: An Amazon EC2 instance belongs to its selected Region. Running copies elsewhere requires explicitly deploying them in those Regions.
cards.misconception: Assuming AWS global infrastructure automatically duplicates regional deployments.

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling distributes incoming application requests among running instances.
cards.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling manages instance capacity. Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming requests among instances.
cards.misconception: Confusing instance capacity management with request distribution.

source.title: Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture

cards.statement: A highly available application requires deployment across multiple AWS Regions.
cards.explanation: A workload can achieve high availability across multiple Availability Zones within one AWS Region.
cards.misconception: Treating a multi-Region deployment as a prerequisite for high availability.

source.title: Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture

cards.statement: Infrastructure as a Service gives customers more system-level control than Software as a Service.
cards.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service exposes infrastructure building blocks for customers to manage; Software as a Service provides a product managed by its provider.

cards.statement: The reliability pillar's primary goal is the efficient use of computing resources.
cards.explanation: Performance efficiency focuses on using computing resources efficiently to meet a workload's performance requirements.
cards.misconception: Assigning the performance efficiency pillar's purpose to reliability.

cards.statement: Encrypting sensitive data supports the security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.
cards.explanation: The security pillar recommends protecting data with encryption, including data being stored and data being transmitted.

cards.statement: The cost optimization pillar's purpose is recovering workloads after infrastructure failures.
cards.explanation: The reliability pillar addresses recovery from failures through practices such as automatic recovery and recovery testing.
cards.misconception: Assigning failure recovery to cost optimization rather than reliability.

cards.statement: The sustainability pillar addresses the environmental impact of running cloud workloads.
cards.explanation: Sustainability considers energy use and resource efficiency to reduce a workload's environmental impact.

cards.statement: The operational excellence pillar encourages teams to learn from day-to-day operations.
cards.explanation: Teams improve operations by learning from operational events and metrics, then sharing those lessons across the organization.

cards.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework recommends testing workloads at production scale.
cards.explanation: On-demand infrastructure lets teams reproduce a production-sized test environment and remove it when testing finishes.

cards.statement: The performance efficiency pillar primarily evaluates the financial value of cloud spending.
cards.explanation: Cost optimization focuses on delivering business value at the lowest price; performance efficiency focuses on effective use of computing resources.
cards.misconception: Confusing financial efficiency with the performance efficiency pillar.

cards.statement: The operational excellence pillar favors frequent changes that are small and reversible.
cards.explanation: Small, reversible changes reduce the impact of a failed change and make it easier to return to a working state.

cards.statement: The security pillar treats perimeter protection as a substitute for layered security controls.
cards.explanation: The security pillar recommends defense in depth: security controls at multiple layers, including networks, applications, and data.
cards.misconception: Assuming perimeter defenses replace protections inside the workload.

cards.statement: An AWS Well-Architected review is a compliance audit of an application's architecture.
cards.explanation: A Well-Architected review is a constructive discussion that identifies architectural risks and opportunities to improve a workload.
cards.misconception: Treating a best-practice architecture review as a compliance audit.

cards.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework supports evolving architecture as business needs change.
cards.explanation: Cloud architectures can evolve as requirements change, rather than being fixed by an early design decision.

cards.statement: The AWS Well-Architected Framework puts cost optimization ahead of reliability in pillar tradeoffs.
cards.explanation: Pillar tradeoffs depend on business needs; a mission-critical workload can justify higher costs to improve reliability.
cards.misconception: Assuming the framework gives cost optimization a fixed priority over reliability.

cards.statement: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations assess their readiness for cloud adoption.
cards.explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations improve cloud readiness and develop a roadmap for transformation.

source.title: An Overview of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

cards.statement: The AWS CAF People perspective focuses on designing the organization's cloud infrastructure.
cards.explanation: In AWS CAF, People addresses culture, leadership, workforce, and organizational change; Platform addresses the cloud platform.
cards.misconception: Confusing the People and Platform perspectives of AWS CAF.

cards.statement: The AWS CAF Governance perspective primarily handles the day-to-day delivery of cloud services.
cards.explanation: In AWS CAF, Operations addresses ongoing service delivery; Governance coordinates cloud initiatives to maximize value and reduce transformation risks.
cards.misconception: Confusing governance of cloud transformation with daily cloud operations.

cards.statement: The AWS CAF Business perspective connects cloud investments to the organization's business outcomes.
cards.explanation: The AWS CAF Business perspective involves leaders such as the chief executive and chief financial officers, who align cloud investment with business goals.

cards.statement: Rehosting moves an application to AWS while preserving its existing application architecture.
cards.explanation: Rehosting transfers an application to cloud infrastructure with minimal application changes, making it a lift-and-shift approach.

cards.statement: Replatforming requires redesigning an application's core architecture for the cloud.
cards.explanation: Replatforming introduces cloud optimizations, such as using a managed database; redesigning the core architecture is refactoring.
cards.misconception: Confusing replatforming with refactoring or re-architecting.

cards.statement: Repurchasing replaces an existing application with another product, such as a SaaS offering.
cards.explanation: Repurchasing switches products instead of moving the existing application, for example by adopting a vendor-hosted software service.

cards.statement: Retiring an application means keeping it in its current environment for later review.
cards.explanation: Retiring decommissions an application; retaining keeps it in its current environment.
cards.misconception: Confusing the retire strategy with the retain strategy.

cards.statement: An organization can choose different migration strategies for applications in the same portfolio.
cards.explanation: Portfolio assessment assigns a migration approach to individual applications, reflecting their circumstances and business value.

source.title: Best practices for assessing applications to be retired during a migration to the AWS Cloud

cards.statement: AWS Database Migration Service supports ongoing replication of changes during a data migration.
cards.explanation: AWS Database Migration Service can copy existing data and replicate subsequent changes to keep the source and target synchronized.

source.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?

cards.statement: Migration Evaluator supports database replication when moving applications into the AWS Cloud.
cards.explanation: Migration Evaluator assesses an existing environment to build a data-driven business case and cost estimates for migration.
cards.misconception: Mistaking a migration assessment service for a data migration service.

cards.statement: The AWS CAF Align phase focuses on expanding successful production pilots across the business.
cards.explanation: In AWS CAF, Scale expands production pilots; Align identifies capability gaps, dependencies, and stakeholder concerns.
cards.misconception: Confusing the Align and Scale phases of cloud transformation.

cards.statement: The base compute charge for an Amazon EC2 On-Demand instance depends on its CPU utilization.
cards.explanation: The base On-Demand compute charge for an Amazon EC2 instance accrues for its running time, including time when the instance is idle.
cards.misconception: Confusing low CPU activity with stopping a billable running instance.

cards.statement: Pay-as-you-go cloud computing replaces upfront infrastructure investment with usage-based expense.
cards.explanation: Cloud consumption shifts spending from buying infrastructure in advance to paying for resources as they are used.

cards.statement: Powering on-premises servers is part of the total cost of owning the infrastructure.
cards.explanation: An on-premises environment has physical operating costs, including electricity for servers, beyond the hardware purchase price.

cards.statement: The Amazon EC2 instance with the lowest hourly price provides the lowest total compute cost for a job.
cards.explanation: Total compute cost depends on price and runtime; a higher-priced instance can cost less overall if it finishes a job sufficiently faster.
cards.misconception: Comparing hourly rates while ignoring how long a workload runs.

cards.statement: Rightsizing reduces cloud costs by committing to a discounted resource usage rate.
cards.explanation: Rightsizing matches resources to workload needs, such as reducing oversized Amazon EC2 instances; usage commitments are a separate savings approach.
cards.misconception: Confusing resource sizing with commitment-based discounts.

source.title: Optimizing your cost with rightsizing recommendations

cards.statement: Automating repeated operational tasks reduces the manual work needed to perform them.
cards.explanation: Effective automation performs routine procedures consistently, reducing manual mistakes as well as operator effort.

cards.statement: AWS achieves economies of scale by aggregating infrastructure demand across many customers.
cards.explanation: Combining demand lets AWS operate infrastructure at greater scale, which can lower the cost of providing resources.

cards.statement: Bring Your Own License bundles the software license charge into the AWS service price.
cards.explanation: Bring Your Own License uses eligible licenses supplied by the customer; license-included pricing bundles the software license with the service.
cards.misconception: Confusing customer-supplied licenses with license-included pricing.

cards.statement: AWS tiered volume pricing bases discounts on a customer's commitment to future usage.
cards.explanation: Tiered volume discounts lower unit prices as eligible consumption grows; commitment discounts are a separate pricing mechanism.
cards.misconception: Confusing usage-volume discounts with future spending commitments.

cards.statement: Using an existing software license on AWS depends on the software vendor's licensing terms.
cards.explanation: Bring Your Own License requires checking the vendor's terms to confirm that the planned cloud deployment is permitted.

cards.statement: Cloud financial management automatically becomes AWS's responsibility after a workload migrates.
cards.explanation: Customers need their own cloud financial management capability to track spending, allocate costs, and optimize business value.
cards.misconception: Assuming moving infrastructure to AWS transfers financial management accountability.

cards.statement: Cost per transaction falls when transaction volume grows faster than the spending needed to serve it.
cards.explanation: Unit cost compares spending with business output; if completed transactions grow faster than spending, the cost per transaction decreases.
